transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I'm completely exhausted by these overwhelming thoughts about germs and contamination that I just can't get out of my head. They force me to spend hours every day washing my hands and cleaning everything, and I feel like I've completely lost control. It's just taking over my entire life and I really need help.
Can you describe a typical situation where you feel the urge to wash your hands or clean, and how do you feel if you're unable to do so?

Whenever I touch public surfaces like doorknobs or handrails, I'm instantly hit with an overwhelming fear that I've been contaminated with dangerous germs. If I'm prevented from washing my hands right away, I feel an intense, suffocating anxiety and absolutely cannot focus on anything else until I can clean them.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and behaviors, and have they interfered with your ability to work, maintain relationships, or engage in activities you enjoy?

I'm not entirely sure how long this has been going on, as it feels like it has been building up for a very long time. I'm also not really sure how much it has interfered with my work or relationships, because everything has just felt so overwhelming and blurred lately.
Are these thoughts about germs and contamination intrusive, meaning they come into your mind unwanted, or are they something you feel are justified and reasonable concerns?

They are definitely intrusive and completely unwanted. I know deep down that these fears aren't reasonable, but they constantly pop into my head and cause me so much distress that I just can't control them.

{
  "category": "differential diagnosis",
  "subcategory": "comorbidities and rule-out",
  "question": "Do you experience any other repetitive thoughts

Yes, I do. I constantly struggle with severe doubts about whether I locked the front door or turned off the stove, and I also get highly distressing, forbidden thoughts that feel completely out of character. Additionally, I have this overwhelming urge that items around me must be lined up perfectly and symmetrically, or I just can't find peace.

Can you estimate how much time you spend each day engaged in these repetitive thoughts and behaviors, such as checking locks, arranging items, and washing your hands, and how do you think they are affecting your overall quality of life?

All of these thoughts and behaviors, like checking, arranging, and washing, definitely take up a massive amount of my time and cause me a lot of distress. I'm not really sure of the exact number of hours, though, as I haven't tracked the precise time each day. It just feels like they occupy my mind almost constantly.
Can you tell me more about these forbidden thoughts that feel out of character, what kind of!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!  thoughts are they and how often do you experience them?

It's really difficult and embarrassing to talk about, but these thoughts happen almost daily and cause me severe anxiety. They involve highly distressing, intrusive ideas about harming people I love, unwanted taboo sexual thoughts, or blasphemous religious images that are completely against my character.

How do you think these obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors are impacting your daily functioning, relationships, and overall well-being, and are you experiencing any significant distress or impairment as a result?

I'm not entirely sure and haven't really thought about how they impact my relationships or functioning in detail. I just know that these thoughts and rituals cause me a lot of general distress and take up a huge amount of my time.

Now that we've discussed your symptoms and their impact on your life, what are your expectations from treatment, and how motivated are you to work on reducing the distress and impairment caused by these obsessive thoughts and compulsive behaviors?

I haven't thought deeply about what specific treatment expectations I have yet. But I am highly motivated to do whatever it takes because I just want to find some relief from these exhausting thoughts and behaviors.

Based on what we've discussed, I think we can work together to develop a treatment plan to help you manage your symptoms and improve your quality of life. Would you be open to exploring cognitive-behavioral therapy, medication, or a combination of both as potential treatment options?

I am definitely open to getting any help that can make this stop, but I am really not sure whether therapy, medication, or a combination of both would be the best option for me. I would really appreciate it if you could share your recommendation on what you think would work best in my situation.
